rail.closed: REST and MCP stay closed until you finish setup.
rail.finished: Setup finished. REST and MCP answer by the access you chose.

welcome.title: Set up Pit Officer
welcome.lead: This wizard sets Officer up for work.
welcome.closedTitle: Officer is closed until setup is finished
welcome.closedBody: Its REST API and MCP answer no program and no agent yet. Nothing is traded and nothing is connected until you set it up.
welcome.backupTitle: Release builds copy the database before every migration
welcome.backupBody: Before a release build migrates an existing database, Officer writes a copy of it beside the file. The panel then offers that copy for download, so that you can keep it.

accounts.title: How many accounts will you use?
accounts.lead: With one account, Officer acts on it only and the panel shows no account fields. The mode can be changed later on the Service page.

funds.title: Check funds before an order?
funds.lead: Officer refuses an order that needs more funds than the account holds, or lets it pass and keeps the accounting. Every policy you set applies in both modes. The mode can be changed later on the Policies page.

encryption.title: Seal stored keys with a master key?
encryption.lead: Officer keeps the keys of your trading connections and data providers, and its own access tokens, in its database file. A master key seals them: a copied database or backup is useless without it. The key can also be set later, at any time.

key.title: With a master key
key.description: Stored keys are sealed. You create the key once and keep a copy.

none.title: Without encryption
none.description: Nothing to do now. Stored keys lie in the file as plain text until a master key is set.

encryption.waiting: Waiting for Officer to come back with the key…
encryption.on: Encryption is on. Officer sealed its database.
encryption.noneTitle: Without encryption, whoever gets the database file gets your keys
encryption.noneWho: Who gets it: anyone who copies the file or a backup - from this disk, a synced folder, a disk image, a lost laptop.
encryption.noneWhat: What they can do: trade through your trading connections, use your data subscriptions, use Officer's own tokens, sign decisions in Officer's name.
encryption.noneBanner: While keys of trading connections or data providers are stored unencrypted, a yellow notice stays at the bottom of the side panel; it leads to the master key setting.
encryption.noneAck: I understand: my keys are stored unencrypted.

signing.title: Sign Officer's decisions?
signing.lead: Officer can sign every decision it issues on an order. A program that executes the order checks the signature and knows the decision came from this Officer, unchanged. Without a signature the decision still goes out, unsigned.

access.title: Who may use Officer?
access.lead: Officer listens only on this computer. That keeps other computers out - not other software on this one.

agent.title: Connect your AI agent
agent.lead: Your agent talks to Officer over MCP. By default it reads and checks orders and changes nothing; allow more on MCP access.
agent.warning: Give the agent this token only - never the API token or the panel password: with those it steps around its MCP limits.
